content:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager: elevated 429/503 rate for /v1/embeddings (prod). Auto-alert triggered at 03:12 UTC for error-rate > 8% sustained over 3m. Paging @sam_oncall.

sam_oncall: ack. I'm on it. First pass — which tenants impacted most?

metrics-bot: quick snapshot: global 429 = 12.8% (03:10-03:13), global 503 = 1.9%. Top tenants by 429 volume: acme-ads-prod (56% of 429s), smartdocs-prod (18%), others small. Latency p50/p95 increased slightly. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/d/embeddings/429-503-live?panelId=3&from=now-15m

nina_sre: thanks. looks correlated with a surge in batch-embedding jobs from acme-ads-prod starting ~03:05. They ramped batch size + concurrent jobs. See histogram of request sizes on the dashboard.

sam_oncall: ok — quick mitigation plan: 1) apply tenant-level QPS cap to acme-ads-prod, 2) disable batch path for that tenant (fall back to streaming endpoint), 3) add temporary routing weight to route ~20% of embedding traffic to lower-cost quantized model to relieve memory pressure. Can someone run the commands?

carlos_support: reaching out to ACME CSM and letting them know we're throttling to reduce errors. I'll paste the message to them once change is live.

deploy-bot: small note: quantized-model-2 has been validated for inference but needs a routing toggle, ready to flip on request.

nina_sre: I'll execute the shaping policies. Running command to set tenant QPS:

```
redwoodctl traffic shape --tenant acme-ads-prod --qps 60 --reason "emergency 429 mitigation" --ttl 30m
```

nina_sre: shaping applied. CLI returned id=shape-8b6. Verifying...

metrics-bot: shaping in effect. acme-ads-prod outgoing QPS dropped from ~4200 to ~58 within 30s. 429 rate for acme-ads-prod went from 21% -> 6.4% in the first minute. Global 429 dropped to 8.1%.

sam_oncall: nice. Now disable batch-embedding path for that tenant:

```
ffctl set acme-ads-prod features.batch_embedding false --actor=sam_oncall --note "disable heavy path while we stabilize"
```

sam_oncall: flag toggled off. traffic shows reduced avg request size.

metrics-bot: after flag flip: p95 token processing time down 12%, queue depth reduced on runtime pool-a. 503 count unchanged so far (still small).

nina_sre: routing weight change next. Applying 20% weight to quantized-model-2 for embedding route:

```
redwoodctl route update embeddings --tenant acme-ads-prod --add-weight quantized-model-2=20 --actor=nina_sre
```

nina_sre: route change applied (rule-id route-zz9). Starting gradual ramp to avoid cold-start penalty.

metrics-bot: within 3m quantized path taking ~18% of acme traffic. Memory pressure on pool-b easing, OOMs gone. acme 429 now 3.2%, global 429 4.5%.

carlos_support: I posted to ACME CSM: "We observed your batch job surge and applied temporary rate shaping and disabled the batch-embedding path to stabilize. We will monitor and follow up in 30m." They asked if this will affect throughput; I told them we'll coordinate rolling back once metrics look stable.

sam_oncall: good. Any signs of collateral customer impact? smartdocs-prod still showing small uptick, but under control. No major 5xx cascades to downstream services.

nina_sre: one incident detail — an autoscaler mis-tuned on pool-a meant it didn't scale fast for high concurrent KV cache allocations, contributing to queuing and 429s. I've filed infra-ticket INF-4127 with immediate note to revisit default autoscale policy.

sam_oncall: are there any jobs still in retry loops causing sustained load?

metrics-bot: we see increased client retries from acme backoff buckets; retry logic is exponential but tight. We could also insert a short header-based reject to reduce client retry pressure while we coordinate with them.

sam_oncall: let's avoid global rejects. For now keep QPS cap and route changes. Next: alert rules — lower thresholds so we catch regression. Nina, can you add a transient alert for acme 429 > 5% for 2m?

nina_sre: adding alert:
```
alertctl create --name "acme-embeddings-429" --expr "acme_429_rate > 0.05" --for 2m --severity critical
```
Alert created.

metrics-bot: alert firing will page if condition holds. I'll also put a dashboard bookmark in runbook.

emily_next_oncall: I'm on shift in ~35m. Sam, any handoff notes to me?

sam_oncall: handoff notes:
- Mitigations applied: tenant QPS cap (shape-8b6) TTL 30m, batch_embedding FF off for acme, 20% routing to quantized-model-2 (route-zz9).
- Observed effect: acme 429 reduced 21% -> 3.2% in ~8m. Global 429 12.8% -> 4.5%.
- Open follow-ups: INF-4127 autoscaler tuning; ENG-7895 evaluate client retry backoff guidance to customers; Support follow-up PRD-1132 with ACME CSM for change window.
- TTLs: shape expires in 30m unless extended; routing change is persistent (we can roll back manually), feature flag off persists until manual re-enable.
- Contact: nina_sre (SRE), carlos_support (CSM), platform-oncall for infra.

emily_next_oncall: thanks — I'll monitor dashboards and extend TTL if safe. If 429 creeps above 5% again, I'll escalate to paging.

sam_oncall: one last thing — adding a short postmortem note in #incidents channel and leaving this thread for context. Also creating a short customer-facing note template for CS to use.

carlos_support: posted message to ACME CSM and added them to a follow-up meeting at 10:00 UTC. They appreciated the proactive throttle.

metrics-bot: final snapshot at 03:42 UTC before handoff: acme 429=2.9%, global 429=3.9%, 503=1.5%. Queue depths normalized.

sam_oncall: handing off to @emily_next_oncall. I'll remain available for 10m if anything spikes. Closing on-call thread for now. :white_check_mark:
